subject: Intermittent streaming freezes & oscillatory chunk gaps — BrightLeaf production (urgent)
messages:
From: Sam Wu <sam.wu@brightleaf.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Customers seeing frequent streaming freezes and chunk gaps

Sergio —

We're seeing a sharp uptick in streaming stalls this morning across multiple clients in us-west. Symptoms: long periods of silence during token streaming (10s+), then a burst of tokens; some clients report a websocket close with 1006 around the same time. Error-rate on our side (application-level) jumped to ~4.5% and throughput dropped ~28% compared to baseline. This started around 08:50 PDT and has persisted with intermittent recovery.

Attached a short HAR and a sample server trace (sample_trace.json). We also captured logs from one of the affected hosts (client_capture.har).

Can you triage? This is impacting our production summarization flows; customers are complaining.

— Sam
Ops Lead, BrightLeaf Analytics
attachments: client_capture.har (application/http-archive), sample_trace.json (application/json)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-28T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming freezes & oscillatory chunk gaps — BrightLeaf production (urgent)

Sam — thanks for the quick report and the traces. I'm pulling Marissa (runtime) and Grace (AM) into the thread. We're treating this as a P1 for BrightLeaf.

Immediate actions we can take to reduce customer impact:
- Route new streams from BrightLeaf to the low-latency model variant (v1-lite) while we triage.
- Push a short-term increase to websocket keepalive and client ping interval to reduce proxy-driven timeouts.
- Enable token-prefix caching for their hot sessions to cut downstream throughput pressure.

Requests for you: sample of 3-5 client connection IDs + timestamps where you saw the 10s silence, and whether the clients are behind a proxy/CDN. Also confirm whether these clients are using chunked transfer over a persistent reverse proxy or direct websocket.

I'll stand up a triage call in 20 minutes if that works for your ops team.

— Sergio
Triage owner (Redwood Inference)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Sam Wu <sam.wu@brightleaf.ai>
Date: 2026-08-28T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming freezes & oscillatory chunk gaps — BrightLeaf production (urgent)

On 2026-08-28 09:26, sergio_alvarez wrote:
> I'll stand up a triage call in 20 minutes if that works for your ops team.

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed behavior in our telemetry: a periodic "chunk-gap" signature where the chunk inter-arrival time spikes (~1.2–12s) then compensating bursts. Correlates with increased upstream proxy 502/504 transient errors in the same window.
- Metrics snapshot (p95): streaming_chunk_gap_rate = 12.1% (baseline 0.6%), stream_error_rate = 4.8% (baseline 0.2%), effective throughput (tokens/s) down ~30%.
- Trace analysis: sample_trace.json shows the model runtime continued generation (no long GC or gpu stall), but the downstream connection experienced heartbeat misses and TCP-level retransmits. Packet capture points to an intermediary (customer-side proxy or cloud load balancer) delaying packets for ~1.5s intermittently.
- Repro: We can reproduce a single stalled chunk by placing a synthetic delay in our nginx upstream (dev test) and it yields the exact observed client symptoms (10s silence then a burst).

Short-term mitigation applied (09:40):
1) We routed incoming BrightLeaf streaming traffic to v1-lite and forced unconditional heartbeat pings at 15s rather than default 45s.
2) Tuned the chunk flush behavior to emit partial chunks when the buffer exceeds 256 bytes (reduces impact of short proxy stalls).

Impact of mitigations (09:55–10:15):
- chunk_gap_rate fell to ~2.7% and client-visible errors dropped below 1.1% for the test cohort.

Next steps (owner):
- Marissa: continue log correlation and provide a packet-level timeline for the largest incidents. (attachment: proxy_logs.txt)
- Sergio: coordinate routing rollback plan and communicate to BrightLeaf PMs/execs.
- Grace: confirm whether BrightLeaf will open a ticket with their infra provider for the suspected intermediary.

Attachments: proxy_logs.txt (text), stream_metrics.csv (text/csv)

— Marissa
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-28T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: BrightLeaf production streaming impact — need exec decision on credits & SLA exceptions

Jonas / Evelyn —

Quick summary: BrightLeaf production customers experienced oscillatory chunk gaps and streaming stalls due to an intermediary proxy causing heartbeat misses. We applied mitigations (routing to v1-lite, forced pings, chunk flush tuning) and saw initial improvement, but this has now become an executive-level conversation:
- Customer impact window: 08:50–10:00 PDT (peak)
- Customers affected: multiple BrightLeaf accounts (production summarization flows)
- Current status: mitigated for routed sessions; root cause likely external proxy owned by BrightLeaf or their cloud provider, but our runtime tuning reduced customer-visible errors.

Requested decisions:
1) Approve a goodwill credit for BrightLeaf (recommendation: 1 month of streaming credits conditional on quick remediation with their infra provider).
2) Approve engineer-on-call extended hours for the next 48 hours for follow-up and monitoring.
3) Approve customer-facing postmortem and a short service bulletin.

I'm happy to hop on a quick call.

— Sergio

- Approve extended EoR on-call for runtime and infra for 48h.

Please prepare a customer-friendly summary and a postmortem stub (timeline, mitigations, RCA hypothesis, next steps). Grace — can you coordinate the customer comms and confirm whether BrightLeaf will open the ticket with their cloud provider?

Jonas

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: BrightLeaf streaming incidents — next steps and postmortem link

Sam —

Thanks again for partnering during the incident. Per our conversation and the team's investigation:
- Short-term mitigations (v1-lite routing, forced pings, chunk flush tuning) are in place and we've seen customer-visible errors fall to <1%.
- RCA hypothesis: intermittent buffering at an intermediary (customer-side proxy or cloud LB) causing heartbeat misses and chunk inter-arrival variability.
- Next steps: BrightLeaf to engage their infra provider and share any ticket numbers; our runtime team will prepare a formal postmortem.

Postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-streaming-postmortem
Ticket opened with BrightLeaf (ref): BL-INC-20260828-01

We'll monitor closely and follow up with a scheduled sync tomorrow to walk through the timeline and mitigation details.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
